output.methodChoice: Read task.md, then collected two items: X1 (26-week history, which gives the normal band the policy uses) and X7 (per-pod metrics for the last five rollouts, which tests the new-vs-old-pod comparison). These two address the Director's two arguments (the "34% jump" and "new pods err twice as much"). Stopped at the 2-item cap. Replica metrics (X2) and the partner-sync interview (X4) were not collected, so H2, H5, R4 and R5 are left as unknown rather than guessed.
output.brief:
Don't roll back v4.18, and don't mute alerting (the page didn't fire; budget use was 0.82x against a 2x trigger).

Last week's 0.41% is an ordinary week for this service. In the previous 26 weeks the average was 0.35%, five weeks were higher (up to 0.51%), and the incident threshold is 0.48%. The 34% jump looks big only because the three weeks before it were unusually quiet. Customers weren't affected (bookings 41.0% to 41.2%, no complaints).

"New pods fail twice as often" isn't evidence against v4.18. Newly started pods always do this: in all five recent rollouts, including a redeploy of unchanged code, new pods ran at 0.47–0.58% against 0.29–0.33% for old ones, because their caches start empty. That's 10–20 extra errors per rollout, versus about 2,200 extra in the week.

I'm confident about "no action now", less about causes: I couldn't test v4.18, Wednesday's replica move or partner-sync's month-end run for small effects.

Next: record the week as normal, keep alerting, and repeat the usual check next week. If it exceeds 0.48% or the page fires, open an incident and look at the replica and partner-sync first.
